summary: A Rust library compiled to WebAssembly and shipped as an npm package with generated TypeScript types, for JavaScript in Node or the browser.
description: Write the fast or tricky part of a JavaScript project in Rust and ship it as an npm package. wasm-bindgen exports functions and a class with TypeScript declarations, options arrive as typed objects, and every failure reaches JavaScript as an Error with a stable code instead of a crash. The logic is tested natively, the exports run as WebAssembly in Node with wasm-bindgen-test, and a TypeScript consumer installs the packed tarball, typechecks it against the generated .d.ts and runs it. The shipped slug functions are the example to replace with your own; publishing stays a person's step.
seoDescription: A Rust WebAssembly recipe: wasm-bindgen and wasm-pack build an npm package with TypeScript types, typed errors, wasm-bindgen-test and a consumer test.

projectExamples.title: Parser shared by browser and server
projectExamples.description: Replace the slug functions with a parser for a file format, so a web page and a Node service validate input with the same compiled code.

projectExamples.title: Image or data transform for a web app
projectExamples.description: Move a slow transform out of JavaScript into Rust, with the inputs and results typed for the TypeScript code that calls it.

plain.whatItIs: A starter for code written in Rust, a fast compiled language, that JavaScript programs install from npm and call like any other package.
goodAt: Running heavy work quickly inside a web page or Node
Sharing one implementation between Rust and JavaScript projects
Typed functions and clear errors for TypeScript callers
notGoodAt: A whole web app or interface; this ships a library other code calls.
Plain JavaScript packages; the TypeScript library stack is simpler.
